issues.claim: Item 110 (b): a raised way is 'RENDERED above what it crosses, with its shadow' (AMENDMENTS-2026-09-28g l. 629); the base states it at §4.3 ('It is drawn above what it crosses, with its shadow', l. 6457), V07's painterly role ('the deck band drawn above everything it crosses', V07 l. 3258) and V09's hit stack ('top first by §8.2's draw order (a raised part above ground part 0)', V09 l. 3253-3254) read it so. In this family the raised way crosses over the wall: a wall laid after a road deck passes beneath its deck (§2.7's laws, law 1 (3), l. 2716-2718; *beneath*, l. 3160: 'No gate on the deck, which passes over the run'), an aqueduct crosses a wall over it on an arch (law 1 (2), l. 2707-2709: 'the band passing beneath the arch'), and a gate, postern or tower stands under an aqueduct's clearing arch (law 1 (5), l. 2724-2725). But §8.2's layer-order table draws raised decks in slot 14 (l. 14147), curtain walls in slot 18 and towers and gate blocks in slot 19 (l. 14152-14153); the order is slot-major across the whole scene (§8.1 item 3, l. 13190-13191) and §8.3's census asserts it ('non-decreasing in the slot table', l. 14261); V01 §5.1.3's hatched order repeats it (V01 l. 3024, 3028-3029; V01 l. 2976-2977), as does §8.2's hatched preset row (l. 14198). Every picture export draws from that list. So wherever a ring is laid under a viaduct (T110-2 (3)'s c14 fixture), an aqueduct crosses a wall over it, or a gate or tower stands under a clearing arch, a builder following §8.2 draws the wall, tower or gatehouse - and the deck's shadow under it - over the deck the model, glTF and CityJSON put above it; a builder following §4.3 draws the deck above and, doing it by order, fails §8.3's census. Two units, two outcomes for one case, one breaking item 110 (b); the census fails the build that keeps the owner's rule (J146, J151: major). No bar catches it: §8.3's item-110 marks row asserts 'every raised deck over the ways it crosses' (l. 14307), ways only.
